sanguinesti-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-.text: Once you're done, press onwards to Varrock and seek an audience with King Roald. Express the desperate nature of the situation here and beg him to send troops.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I don't suppose you would fancy popping in and seeing him, would you?

steps.player: Oh, Veliaf asked me to pay him a visit, actually. I guess I could go and meet with him.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That would be very good indeed. Your king commends you!

Actually, that's a bit odd isn't it? Because in Morytania, strange is the order of the day. I'd have been more surprised if there had been reports of things getting back to normal!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.text: I'm glad you're keeping your sense of humour. It will help you to maintain mental clarity while dealing with the tasks you've been given.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.player: Well there's no shortage of tasks for me. Once I'm done here I have to go and speak to King Roald, or rather, Roald. We've been on first name terms for quite a while now. Funny that, eh?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel.text: Ivan mentioned that he heard some strange noises recently out in front of the temple. Could you have a look and make sure there's nothing funny going on?

options.text: When and where were these noises heard?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Ivan said he heard them throughout the day, but usually when things were very quiet. We both looked around near the temple but we didn't find anything.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: We were both a bit nervous about going any further west than the steps.

steps.player: Do you think the noises could have come from beyond the steps? I mean, from further west?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It's certainly possible and more than likely. I'd be grateful if you could extend your search as wide as you can.

options.text: Did you hear the noises as well?

steps.text: They didn't sound human!

steps.player: Right! That's different! What did they sound like?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Very gruff. almost animal-like in fact.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Other locals have reported seeing shadowy figures in the Silvaria pass. Could just be an enterprising, though perhaps ruthless, bunch of brigands. If it is, simply give them a taste of Misthalin law and order.

steps.player: And if it turns out to be more than that?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well then, my friend, I will pray that Saradomin's blessings be upon you and that he guides your actions and keeps you safe from harm.

steps.player: How incredibly reassuring!

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Don't take that tone with me! Saradomin's powers are not to be underestimated.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Both his parents died in the Sanguinesti region, though he still holds hope that they may be found alive.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The death of Sani has really affected him as well. Like him, she was an orphan. They had a lot in common.

steps.player: It's all so tragic. I wish there was something I could do for him.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well, you brought him here, which was very brave. He's very grateful to you. It's remarkable, really. He has this inner calmness that I find so very affecting.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: His studies go well and he has Saradomin's blessings, it's clear to see. I would see him as a worthy successor as protector of Paterdomus. When all of his teachings are done, naturally.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Yes. And I have some news!
I was attacked near the temple! On the other side of the Salve!
By beasts! From Morytania, I believe. Perhaps werewolves.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: The vampyres must be behind this! Did you speak with Roald yet? We need his support if we are to end this suffering.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Not yet, I'm afraid. I thought you would want to know about the werewolves as soon as possible.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: It's good of you to return with this information, but we need to know Roald's answer before we can make any further plans.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [playername]. Did you find anything out nearby?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Not clearly, but I believe they could have been werewolves.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: This is terrible, terrible news! They have found a way to get across the Salve!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: I must make immediate preparations and meet with other members of my order. You must hurry directly to King Roald and impart this information to him.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Here, take these runes. They should help you to return to Varrock faster.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Very well, I'll make my way to Varrock and bid you good luck.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [playername]. Have you been to Varrock yet?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Not yet, sorry. What should I do again?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: You need to warn King Roald about possible incursions into Misthalin from Morytania.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: Ah yes, quite right. Thanks for reminding me.

options.text: Talk to the king about Morytania.

steps.player: I must speak with you on a matter of grave importance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Certainly. What seems to be the problem?

steps.player: I've witnessed a great many terrible things happening in Morytania, some of which could be happening in Misthalin before long!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This sounds pretty grave, please go on.

steps.player: I have been helping a collection of brave freedom fighters called the Myreque for some time now. They've been fighting against the vampyres and their ruler, Lowerniel Drakan.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: We're all too aware of Drakan and his vampyres. What risk do they pose to Misthalin though?

steps.player: In Morytania, Drakan and his kin farm humans for their blood! People, my lord, like your own loyal subjects!
It's not just the citizens of Morytania at risk though. It seems that werewolves have been kidnapping people from this side of the Salve to be used as blood tithes for the vampyres!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This is awful! Yes, yes of course, we must do something!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: I would beg my lord not to give in so easily to his very compassionate nature. We know not if these people are loyal Saradomin supporters, my liege.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Oh yes, we need to consider that as well. You're right of course, Aeonisig. Do you know if these people follow Saradomin?

steps.player: I am not certain, but surely this isn't the issue? They are in dire need...

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: As are many, my young friend. Is the king meant to leave Misthalin unguarded on the whim of some errant adventurer?

steps.player: But you don't understand! It's not just about the people of Morytania. Like I say, there were werewolves in Misthalin!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I dare say you gave fight and slaughtered the foul beasts where they stood!

steps.player: I'm sad to say that I did not. I had no chance. I was knocked unconscious before I could properly react. Please, Misthalin must come to the aid of the people of Morytania.
The Myreque cannot fight this battle against the vampyres by themselves!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, yes! I will ready my army and prepare to enter Morytania via Paterdomus. Morytania has for too long threatened the borders of Misthalin.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: My lord, this course of action will lead to very severe consequences! Your interference in Morytania will likely upset the balance and could send the world into another cataclysmic God War.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But Drakan has invaded Misthalin! I must respond!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: There is no proof that Drakan has invaded Misthalin, my lord!

steps.player: Yes there is! I saw it with my own eyes!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Being knocked out by agents unknown does not constitute evidence. In fact, it's something that the most inexperienced of local folk could accomplish!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But I can't just stand here and do nothing, Aeonisig! I must try to help if I can.

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: I am afraid with the Guthixian edicts regarding religious balance, there is little else we can do.

steps.player: Guthixian edicts?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Indeed. They were put in place by Guthix himself at the end of the God Wars. At least, so his followers claim. All of us must abide by them, lest the world fall into ruin again.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: What a load of tosh!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: An apt description, my lord. The edicts are likely to be little more than propaganda created by the followers of Guthix.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Well then what's the issue?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: The edicts need closer study before we can be sure.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: But that will take ages, we need to act now!

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: As you say, it will take some time. We now pay the price for our lack of foresight in letting Guthixian edicts restrict the might of Saradomin's will.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Yes, yes, but we can start to make amends for that now, can't we?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Yes sire, there are some papers to sign, but essentially we can start work on this right away.

steps.player: Signing papers! Is that the sum of the aid that Misthalin can provide to Morytania?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Hold your disrespectful tongue! How dare you address the king in that way? We should throw you in the stocks!

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: I am sorry, but Aeonisig is my advisor, and what he says, while it pains me, is the truth. However, I will enact a mercenary protocol.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: This will allow all able-bodied men to fight in the defence of Misthalin for glory and spoils. You will find that many sword arms from Misthalin should soon join the resistance force.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: In the meantime, we will look into the Guthixian edicts and find a way to rid ourselves of Drakan for good.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: That is for you to decide, but I would assume that you'd want to report back to your comrades in Morytania.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: If they're relying on support from Misthalin, you'll need to let them know that it might take some time before that happens.

steps.player: So I came all this way for nothing?

steps.speaker: Aeonisig Raispher
steps.text: Is it nothing then to have an audience with the king? Your lack of respect astonishes me. How you have survived so long with such disgraceful manners is nothing short of a miracle!

steps.player: Sorry. I had just hoped for so much more.

steps.text: Well then, I must try to do something to satisfy you. I will have my advisor Aeonisig teleport you to Paterdomus so that you are more quickly on your way. Will you accept my offer?

Why can't you send troops to Morytania?

steps.player: Why can't you send troops to Morytania?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The Guthixian edicts supposedly exist to ensure a balance is kept when it comes to religious and spiritual beliefs in the world. At the moment, things are considered to be in balance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Misthalin is a Saradominist region, but Morytania is filled with creatures of Zamorak. A war between our two regions would be considered a war between Saradomin and Zamorak.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: If I send troops to Morytania, there is risk that the balance will be disrupted. Many followers of Guthix are apparently bound by oath to fight to keep the balance.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It is said that when all three sides are joined in war, Guthix will 'reawaken and remake the world without mercy for the pain of beast or man.'

steps.player: Is that really true?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Personally, I don't think so. However, Aeonisig does not feel we should risk it until we can do further research on the Guthixian edicts.

steps.player: What is a mercenary protocol?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It means that people can fight with the blessings of the king in defence of the kingdom.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Normally, if a force is amassed, they may be considered a threat to Misthalin's national security. We'd have to send the army to disband them.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: However, a mercenary protocol allows a group to form a mercenary company. They are allowed certain rights so long as they operate within the law.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: The Guthixian edicts prevent us from doing too much at this point, but this situation in Morytania requires some action. Unfortunately, this is the best thing I can think of at the moment.

options.text: When can you send aid to Morytania?

steps.player: When can you send aid to Morytania?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: It depends on how long it takes the Church of Saradomin to read through the Guthixian edicts and return with an answer on how to proceed.

steps.player: What part does Guthix play in all this?

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Guthixian edicts rule over those of all other religions. Many followers of Guthix claim that the edicts have largely controlled the peace that Misthalin has experienced for so many years.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: Apparently, some followers of Guthix have sworn an oath to perform ceremonies to try and re-awaken Guthix if the edicts are broken.

steps.speaker: King Roald
steps.text: They say that peace and tolerance are needed to maintain the balance. I've no doubt it's all a load of rubbish, but we can't proceed until we are sure.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Talk to the king about Morytania.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Hello, [player name]. Have you been to Varrock yet?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.player: I have. King Roald isn't able to send troops for our fight against the Drakans. Apparently, some Guthixian edicts need to be scrutinised in more detail or else the balance will be affected?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.speaker: Drezel
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-drezel-af.text: Oh dear! I once did some studying of the edicts. I can see why the king and his advisors are cautious.

steps.player: What should I do now?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The Myreque will need to know all that you have experienced so far. You should report to Veliaf when you can.

options.text: Can you explain a little about the Guthixian edicts?

steps.player: Can you explain a little about the Guthixian edicts?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well, only a little. The followers of Guthix make all sorts of wild claims where he is involved. Those of us who serve Saradomin know that these claims are mostly baseless.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: What we do know is that Guthix is a god of nature and balance. We believe him to be of average power. Enough to pay attention to, but nothing compared to the strength of Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It is said that long ago, back when the gods walked these lands with us, a great war was fought called the God Wars.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The stories say the war lasted for thousands of years and that the carnage saw the world forever changed.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The followers of Guthix claim that this war ended when Guthix awoke from his slumber and banished the other gods, leaving the world to mortals.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: This is likely not the true version of events. Guthixians also claim that it was Guthix himself who made the world. Obviously, that is not correct.

steps.player: So where do these edicts come in?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: They were apparently created at the end of the God Wars to ensure that the world never sees a conflict like that again.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: The edicts state that no single god should be allowed to gain enough power to become dominant. Instead, a balance must be kept between the gods and their servants.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: If the balance is not kept, the followers of Guthix will try to intervene. If they are unable to restore balance, they will supposedly awaken Guthix from his slumber beneath the earth.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Once he awakens, they say he will remake the world, destroying civilisation as we know it.

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: It's just a story of course. All made up by the Guthixians to help them feel relevant.

steps.player: But if the edicts are just made up, what's the risk?

steps.speaker: Drezel
steps.text: Well when there's threats of the world being remade, you can't be too careful. It is wise to be cautious. After all, wisdom is one of Saradomin's greatest strengths.

steps.player: Okay, thanks.

options.text: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.player: Can you tell me why you're here?

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Of course. I plan to assist the forces of Saradomin who will come to our aid, and fight against the legions of vampyres that infest this foul place. These brave mercenaries shall need a guide.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: When a guide arrives, I will aid the mercenary by holding their wealth for their eventual return. The mercenary will repay the guide by giving him a token for items which I am holding.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: I shall give such items to the guide as payment for their services once I'm handed the token.

steps.player: What items will you hold?

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Oh, the range of items is very varied. Mercenaries tend to hold raw materials in high esteem and so will deposit those with me. They also seem to be good bartering items.

steps.speaker: Hiylik Myna
steps.text: Generally, things like uncooked lobsters, coal, silver bars, bow strings. Things which are useful! Plus the odd tome of experience, which are considered incredibly useful.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: King Roald cannot send troops! I talked to him at great length and was unable to persuade him. His Saradominist advisor cited Guthixian edicts as the reason for not sending aid.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: Guthixian edicts? How do they prevent Roald from sending troops?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Apparently a war in Morytania will risk disturbing the balance between Saradomin and Zamorak so the Guthixians will need to intervene.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: There has long been a desire by the Church of Saradomin to see Guthixian power eroded away. This stinks of politics. They're just using the situation here for their own gain!

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: Roald did agree to enact a mercenary protocol. He said it was the best he could offer for the moment without contravening the Guthixian edicts.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: Well that's something I guess. Not exactly what we were hoping for though.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.player: What should we do now? There must be someone else we can turn to?

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz
misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-hu.text: We must inform the Sanguinesti order of the Myreque of these events. Please go as fast as you can back to the Meiyerditch hideout and forward this information to them.

misthalin-diplomacy-talking-to-veliaf-ag.speaker: Veliaf Hurtz

(Vanstrom and the player fight, with the player unable to hit through Vanstrom's protection. The player is knocked out after taking five hits.)

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Sorry for the interruption, Lord Vanstrom, but Lady Vanescula 'requests' that this individual be questioned before being used as a punch bag.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Vanstrom Klause
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: I take no orders from food sacks like you, Guile. Attend to this yourself. In any case, [he/she] wasn't much of a punch bag anyway.
Vanstrom departs

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Awaken! There are things for you to know.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: Your life may be forfeit but for now you live. My mistress will understand my motives. She has an interest in the one called Safalaan.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: As a gesture for my intervening on your behalf, I'd take it as a kindness if you would deliver a message to him.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: The message you will find secreted behind tiles where smoke is carried away from the depiction of statuesque evil.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.speaker: Sarius Guile
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-sketchin.text: And now be away, but forget not the task that Safalaan set you! For why else would you be here?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: What?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: He came out of nowhere! I tried to fight back, but I just couldn't hurt him.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Brave, very brave. He didn't follow you here did he?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: No, I'm pretty sure I wasn't followed. So anyway, during the fight, Vanstrom knocked me to the floor and I thought I was done for. But then a woman named Sarius showed up.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Sarius? Vanescula Drakan's servant? Hmmm, interesting. Was Vanescula herself nearby?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: No, I saw Vanescula earlier, but when I saw Sarius arrive, Vanescula wasn't around. Sarius told Vanstrom that Vanescula wanted to interrogate me. So Vanstrom got angry and flew away.
Sarius then told me about a message which was meant for you. Something about 'smoke and statues'? She said that Vanescula was interested in you for some reason?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Well, [player name], you certainly seem to have had a very close call. Thanks for letting me know all of this. It's all highly interesting.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Oh, and I almost forgot. Do you have the sketches?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: You have my gratitude, friend! Myreque prevail! I need to take a good look at these and see what we can learn.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: What should I do now?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: Hmm, good question. Didn't you mention something about Sarius and a message?

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: That's right. If I remember correctly, she said it was hidden 'behind tiles where smoke is carried away from the depiction of statuesque evil'.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.text: A riddle? Clearly she doesn't want the message to be easily found. I'd appreciate it if you could look into this further.

close-encounters-with-vyre-kind-talking-.player: I'll see what I can do.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: We should keep an eye out for this place. In fact, it would be great if you could look for it for us. Keep the message. It may help you to locate the laboratory.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: Myreque prevail!

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: Well that message you brought me had some details regarding a laboratory. Maybe there is some information there which could help us.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.player: Where do you think this laboratory could be?

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: It's a good question, but not one I have an answer for. The message seemed to have some hints though. If you get a chance could you look into this for us?

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.player: I'll see what I can do.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.player: Well, whatever it is, someone went to a lot of trouble to try and hide it.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: I can believe that, [player name]. Once again you have our gratitude. For my part, your arrival has not come soon enough. I have a feeling that your efforts in our struggle are not yet over.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: I for one would be grateful for your continued assistance. Together we can pull back the darkness of Hallowvale.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.player: I'll do what I can, Safalaan. You have my support.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: Then I must beg you for one more small task, to return to Veliaf with a message to advise him of what has transpired here.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: I realise that bearing messages seems somewhat lowly, but your ability to pass in and out of the city without being detected makes you perfect for this assignment.

in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.speaker: Safalaan Hallow
in-search-of-statuesque-evil-talking-to-.text: I also have some information which should help with your journeys through Meiyerditch. There are two doors, one is in sector one and the other is in sector two. You can use them to reach this hideout faster.
